target_name: Brand Knowledge With Full Composite Conservatism
rationale: A coherent but purely combinatorial merge of two already-evaluated gen-8 winners (brand-inclusive hidden capital + net-of-liabilities recognition + SUMRANK conservatism), and since it still requires oancf plus a five-year accrual history it will inherit the ~0.07 coverage weakness it does not address, so the expected information gain over its parents is modest.

The coverage-repair motivation is legitimate and the design is falsifiable, but SUMRANK of a persistent variable with its own five-year TS_RANK is largely self-redundant and cannot literally "capture the same information as" the earnings-minus-cash accrual composite, so the stated equivalence claim is overreaching even if the test is worth running.

target_name: Ranked Net Invisible Capital With Brand
rationale: By the proposer's own admission the RANK transform leaves the portfolio sort unchanged, so this is the archived Net Invisible Capital Score with advertising added — a single-ingredient variant whose alpha is near-guaranteed to replicate — and the underlying construct is close to a linear blend of two published anomalies (R&D/intangible capital and the net-operating-assets/working-capital accrual effect) rather than a genuine cross-theme interaction.

target_name: Net Invisible Capital With Reporting Restraint
rationale: Pairing a cumulative stock measure of recognition with a flow measure of current accrual stretch is economically defensible and the Sharpe-based falsification criterion is stated in advance, though the two legs overlap conceptually (the stock score already nets out working-capital accruals) so partial redundancy is likely.

This is the archived "Hidden Capital With Own-History Restraint" with xrd replaced by xrd+xad — a single mechanical ingredient swap of exactly the type already run in gen 8 — offering minimal incremental economic content and a highly predictable result.

target_name: Asset-Anchored Brand Knowledge With Net Recognition
rationale: The deflator-robustness question is fair, but the stated coverage motivation is internally inconsistent — the MAX(ceq, che) floor already handles negative book equity and the parent signal already achieves 0.116 coverage — so the only real change is a scaling choice, and subtracting intan in the numerator while including it in the `at` denominator further muddies the interpretation.
